anchor.quote: Let $n$ be the length of the input sequence, the number of its entries
The input sequence is $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$, a list of complex numbers.
Here $j$ indexes the input entries and runs from $0$ to $n-1$.
Here $k$ indexes the output entries and runs over the same range.
The output sequence is $\hat a = (\hat a_0, \dots, \hat a_{n-1})$

anchor.note: Big-O notation, covered by the profile (big-O notation and worst-case time).
Logarithms, covered by the profile's undergraduate computer science background.

gaps.quote: Each $\hat a_k$ is the value at $\omega^k$ of the polynomial whose coefficient list is $a$.
gaps.note: The page never states the polynomial, nor that a_j is the coefficient of x^j. The reader cannot check that the output entry equals the evaluation at omega^k without this convention.

gaps.term: distinctness of the powers of a primitive root
gaps.quote: the powers $\omega^0,\dots,\omega^{n-1}$ are $n$ distinct $n$-th roots of unity
gaps.note: The page asserts distinctness without argument. It needs that a primitive n-th root has no smaller positive power equal to 1; the page only links the definition of primitive and does not show this consequence.

gaps.term: fast algorithms in O(n log n)
gaps.quote: Fast algorithms compute the same output in $O(n \log n)$ operations.
gaps.note: The page gives no algorithm, no link and no citation for the existence of an O(n log n) method, so the reader cannot check this claim.
